issue.title: Count monitors and post-handoff family shells against max_running_agents
issue.description: A running sase agent holds exactly one runner slot for as long as any of its shells is alive — including its monitor proc shells and every agent shell launched after a monitor handoff — so max_running_agents is the real ceiling on concurrent agents on this host, and every surface that reports occupancy agrees with the admission gate.

issue.title: Occupancy rule and live admission gate
issue.description: count: separate slot occupancy from slot admission in the pure runner-slot core, make a serial agent family hold one slot while any of its shells (agent or monitor) is live, and wire the live admission gate to the new count.

issue.title: Occupancy parity across ACE and agent listings
issue.description: display: make the ACE capacity chip, statistics methodology text, wait modal, and agent listings report the same occupancy the admission gate enforces, including rows for post-handoff family shells that are invisible today.

issue.title: Rust core parity for historical runner occupancy
issue.description: stats: update the duplicated runner-eligibility predicate in the sase-core Rust crate so the Statistics runner-occupancy analysis uses the same rule as live admission, then release the binding and repin it here.

issue.title: Documentation sweep and cross-surface consistency check
issue.description: docs: retire the "serial family follow-ups do not consume slots" claim everywhere it appears, document the sase-agent occupancy rule and the monitor handoff, and verify every surface agrees end to end.

LANDED. All four phases verified against the source and their commits, integration checked, follow-ups routed.

VERIFICATION (step 1). Read every child note and confirmed each against the code and the epic's four commits (63accbfc9 sase-ps.1, 746c80705 sase-ps.3, f9a1afae7 sase-ps.2, 5bb381f4a sase-ps.4).
- count: src/sase/core/runner_slots/_admission.py has the split exactly as planned. is_runner_slot_user_agent_record is documented as admission-only and unchanged; is_runner_slot_occupying_record ignores lineage and is monitor-aware ("started" is a recorded pid when agent_meta.monitor_id is set, otherwise run_started_at); runner_slot_family_key groups by (project_name, agent_family-or-timestamp); running_agent_slot_count charges one slot per family with any occupying serial member plus one per live parallel member. run_agent_wait_slots.py:235 sources running_count from it and the serial-family early return is untouched. running_root_agent_count has no remaining reference anywhere in src/, tests/, docs/, or the Rust crate -- the rename left no second definition of "how many slots are in use", as the plan required.
- display: agent_runner_slots.py reuses the Agents-tab lane projection (sase_agent_status_counts) rather than a third predicate, with a documented narrow supplement for a sequential container whose display status mirrors a terminal child. running_listing._runner_slot_holder_dirs credits one representative shell per serial family and each parallel member, and _is_visible_runner_slot_child now follows occupancy so a post-handoff shell is never missing from sase agent list. The Statistics methodology row and runners legend state the new rule.
- stats: the Rust half is committed on sase-core master as 769b9bc ("fix(agent_stats): count family shells in historical runner occupancy"), not left uncommitted as the phase note warned. agent_runtime.rs carries is_runner_slot_occupying_record, running_agent_slot_count, merge_family_occupancy_intervals, and occupancy_member_start; both crate changelogs list it under [Unreleased]. The sase-core-rs pin stays >=0.27.18,<0.28.0 on purpose: Justfile:112 documents that dev and CI installs build from the checkout and tools/ratchet_core_window moves the published window on the release branch.
- docs: no "serial family follow-ups do not consume slots" claim survives anywhere in docs/ or src/. configuration.md#max_running_agents, ace.md, xprompt.md, llms.md, getting_started.md, troubleshooting/runner-slots.md, monitors.md ("Runner slots"), and default_config.yml all state the occupancy rule and keep holding-a-slot separate from waiting-for-one. The remaining "do not consume" sentences are the correct ones (dependency/time/fork waiters, and a shell parked at QUESTION).
- No feature flag was added, as the plan directed.

LIVE CROSS-SURFACE CHECK. On a busy host: gate running_agent_slot_count = 10; sase agent list -j runner_slots_in_use = 10 across 31 rows, with 10 distinct runner_slot_holders including the monitor sase-pq.land--mon-0 and a post-handoff shell. The gate and the listing agree exactly, which is the property the epic existed to create.

INTEGRATION (step 2). Reviewed every non-epic commit from 63accbfc9 to a2357e214. The two monitor-rendering commits (9102c9efb amber MONITOR phase label, 845253505 settled-monitor gear count) both landed before the display phase and are rendering-only, so they neither duplicate nor conflict with occupancy. Nothing else touches runner slots. Confirmed no surface still computes occupancy independently: integrations/agent_list_entries.py sums the holds_runner_slot flag that running_listing sets from the shared per-family dedup, and axe/chop_policy.py's agent_runners inhibit provider reads that same flag through list_running_agents(), so both inherit the new rule automatically -- which is what makes configuration.md's claim that agent_runners counts "the same population" true rather than aspirational. Every lineage check left in src/ (naming, editor-helper rosters, child summaries, done-row adaptation) is a family lookup, not an occupancy count.
